title: Long-range Nonlinear Sigma Model for a Singular Quantum Kicked Rotor
abstract: Singular kicked rotors have long been compared with power-law random banded matrices (PRBM) because their momentum-space Floquet matrix elements decay algebraically. However, it has remained unclear whether the deterministic correlations of the rotor become irrelevant at long distances and, consequently, under what conditions the two systems share the same infrared theory. To address this question, we derive a nonlocal supersymmetric nonlinear sigma model directly from a quantum kicked rotor with a power-law or logarithmic singularity. By carrying out the renormalization-group analysis up to two-loop order, we show that, after matching the symmetry class and coupling convention, the rotor reproduces the long-range Anderson transition of the corresponding PRBM, including its localized, critical, and extended infrared regimes.
summary: This work rigorously analyzes the spectral properties of a singular quantum kicked rotor by mapping it onto a nonlinear sigma model. Using advanced renormalization group techniques, the authors demonstrate that the rotor's dynamics fall into the same universality class as power-law random banded matrices. This resolves a key theoretical question regarding the relevance of deterministic correlations in the context of Anderson localization.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether the deterministic correlations of a singular quantum kicked rotor become irrelevant at long distances, determining if it shares the same infrared theory as power-law random banded matrices (PRBM).
main_result: The rotor successfully reproduces the long-range Anderson transition of the corresponding PRBM in the localized and critical regimes after appropriate matching of symmetry and coupling conventions.
method: The authors derive a nonlocal supersymmetric nonlinear sigma model from the rotor and perform a detailed renormalization-group (RG) analysis up to two-loop order.
model_or_system: The system is a singular quantum kicked rotor, whose dynamics are governed by a Floquet operator. It is mathematically compared to PRBM, which are characterized by algebraically decaying momentum-space matrix elements.
key_observables: Inverse participation ratios (IPR), two-level quasienergy correlator, and the analysis of localization/critical/extended infrared regimes.
important_parameters: The singularity type (power-law or logarithmic), the RG flow parameters (stiffness $t$, local moment renormalization $Z_p$), and the symmetry class.
main_assumptions: The analysis requires matching the symmetry class, coupling convention, and asymptotic scaling window between the rotor and the PRBM.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by deriving the sigma model, performing RG analysis on correlation functions (like the two-level correlator), and analyzing the flow equations for key parameters like stiffness and local moment renormalization.
why_interesting: The connection between deterministic, structured quantum dynamics (the rotor) and the universality class of random matrix theory (PRBM) provides deep insights into the role of correlations in localization phenomena, relevant for understanding disordered quantum systems.
